title: Stock Market Update: Stocks Cut Weekly Gains
text:
Stocks Cut Weekly Gains 09-Nov-18 13:05 ET Dow -240.54 at 25950.68, Nasdaq -141.73 at 7389.35, S&P -31.82 at 2775.15
[BRIEFING.COM] The S&P 500 struggles with a loss of 1.0%, as investors continue to digest yesterday's policy directive from the Fed, which showed that the central bank remains on a path of gradual tightening. The Dow Jones Industrial Average is down 0.8%, the Nasdaq Composite is down 1.8%, and the Russell 2000 is down 1.8%.
The Producer this will stoke strengthen the Fed's case for additional rate hikes.
Within the S&P sectors, the information technology (-1.8%), materials (-1.6%), and communication services (-1.5%) groups underperform the broader market.
Chip stocks have led the tech sector lower after key Apple (AAPL 203.49, -5.00, -2.4%) supplier Skyworks Solutions (SWKS 76.98, -6.47, -7.8%) issued Q1 earnings and revenue below consensus. Its lower guidance extends a disappointing trend from many semiconductor companies that have warned of weakening chip demand. Likewise, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index underperforms with a loss of 2.1%.
High-growth communication services components Facebook (FB 145.32, -2.56, -1.7%), Netflix (NFLX 303.37 ,-14.75, -4.7%), and Alphabet (GOOG 1059.63, -22.73, -2.1%) weigh down the group. CenturyLink (CTL 18.81, -2.26) also underperforms with a loss of 10.8% after the telecom company missed top and bottom line estimates.
Investors have taken a defensive-approach today, as defensive-oriented sectors outperform and U.S. Treasuries rise. The consumer discretionary and utilities sectors are the only groups in the green with respective gains of 0.4% and 0.1%. Also, the 2-yr yield and 10-yr yield are down four basis points each to 2.93% and 3.19%, respectively.
In other corporate news, Walt Disney (DIS 118.33, +2.35) is up 2.0% after it beat both top and bottom line estimates, while General Electric (GE 77.28, -6.13) has dropped 8.1% after JPMorgan cut its price target on the stock to $6 from $10. General Electric defended itself, saying
Separately, WTI crude has continued to fall today, as it extends steep losses from its October 3 high of $76.90/bbl. Crude is currently down 1.2% at $59.93/bbl. On a related note, the oil-sensitive energy sector has shed 0.6%.
